name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Tuesday 9 September 1975

clue.text: Native finds vessel containing Greek letter

indicators.note: something containing another holds it inside, so the letter sits within the vessel

blocks.note: a tin is a metal container
the second letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A local person discovers a pot with some Greek writing inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A person born in Tibet is a Tibetan, so the word names a native of that Himalayan country.

clue.text: Sort of cricket Pandit Nehru arranged? Not he! .

indicators.note: not he says that the pronoun he must be struck out of the name
arranged means set out in order, so the remaining letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Did India's prime minister organise a kind of cricket match? No, not him.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove HE from the leader's name, then rearrange what is left. Tip-and-run is an informal cricket game in which batsmen must run whenever they hit the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-and-run is a casual form of cricket in which the batter must run after every hit.

clue.text: Slow rail journey through the bush?

blocks.note: British Rail, the former national railway
surface padding that describes the walk: an amble is slow
an amble is a leisurely walk or stroll

explanation.surface: A sluggish train ride through the outback.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, Britain's state railway until the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: A bramble is a prickly shrub such as the blackberry, so it is a kind of bush.

clue.text: Merton hid wreck in Norwegian port

indicators.note: to wreck something is to smash it up, so these letters are broken and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Merton concealed a shipwreck in a harbour in Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan reads Merlon, but the anagram needs a T, so the printed word is Merton.
explanation.definitionFit: Trondheim is a city and harbour on a fjord in central Norway, so it is a Norwegian port.

clue.text: Alaskan scene of my absenteeism?

blocks.note: absence of something is having none of it
my points to the speaker, me

explanation.surface: A place in Alaska where the speaker went missing from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My absenteeism' is read as the speaker not being there, NO ME, with the words taken in reverse order.
explanation.definitionFit: Nome is a town on the Seward Peninsula in Alaska, famous for its gold rush, so it is a scene or setting there.

clue.text: Condescends to include old Bob in plans

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so the coin goes within the verb

blocks.note: deigns means stoops or condescends
a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s

explanation.surface: Someone graciously agrees to fit an old-fashioned bob into the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob is slang for the shilling, a pre-decimal British coin written as s.
explanation.definitionFit: Designs and plans are synonyms as nouns for intended schemes or drawings worked out in advance.

clue.text: Resolute character of 20 joined Pole in exploit

indicators.note: the character of something is its make-up, so the letters of that entry are composed afresh
joined says the pole letter is attached straight after the rearranged letters
in places all of this inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a deed is a feat or exploit
the answer to 20 across
north, one pole of the earth

explanation.surface: A strong-willed person from the bishop's clue teamed up with a Pole for a daring venture.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 20 across are rearranged, the pole letter added, and the lot placed inside the exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: Determined and resolute are synonymous adjectives describing someone firm of purpose and unwavering.

clue.text: Price of course includes very little for this worker

indicators.note: includes means takes within itself, so the small word goes inside

blocks.note: the starting price, the odds offered at a racecourse
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: The cost of a course of study barely leaves anything for the labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is the bookmaker's starting price at a race course; a sweep cleans chimneys.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney sweep is a labourer who cleans soot from flues, hence a worker.

clue.text: Nutty librettist?

blocks.note: surface reading: an eccentric writer of opera words
setter's reading: the Savoy Opera librettist whose surname is one letter off filbert, a hazelnut

explanation.walkthrough: W. S. Gilbert wrote the words for Sullivan's comic operas; his name differs by one letter from filbert, a hazelnut, hence 'nutty'.
explanation.definitionFit: W. S. Gilbert wrote the texts for the Savoy operas, the comic works composed by Arthur Sullivan.

clue.text: Declines to have writing material aboard

blocks.note: aboard means on a ship, abbreviated SS for steamship, and the material goes inside it
ink is used for writing

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to take paper and pens on board.
explanation.walkthrough: Being aboard means being in SS, the abbreviation for a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink and to decline both mean to go down or deteriorate, as in falling health.

clue.text: Instrument with instruction for player

blocks.note: first meaning: the keyboard instrument
second meaning: the score marking telling a musician to play softly

explanation.surface: A musical instrument arrives with directions for whoever plays it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the keyboard instrument and is also the Italian score marking meaning softly, an instruction to a musician.

clue.text: Mead fuddled them - Nigel too

indicators.note: fuddled means muddled by drink, so the letters are confused into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The mead got them drunk, and Nigel as well.
explanation.walkthrough: METHEGLIN is a spiced mead from Wales; the drinking surface fits the answer neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Metheglin is a spiced variety of the honey drink, traditionally Welsh, so it is a kind of mead.

clue.text: Pooter's spirit?

blocks.note: surface reading: the character or soul of Charles Pooter, the hero of a comic Victorian diary
setter's reading: Pooter's book is The Diary of a ___, and a spirit is a being with no physical form

explanation.walkthrough: Mr Pooter is the self-important clerk of the Grossmiths' novel The Diary of a Nobody; a ghost or spirit literally has no body.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooter is famously the insignificant diarist of that comic novel, and a disembodied spirit is literally without a physical form.

clue.text: Unusually large issue of notes

blocks.note: first meaning: three babies born at one birth
second meaning: groups of three musical notes played in the time of two

explanation.surface: An exceptionally big print run of banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring, and three children at once is a large birth; in music the same word means groups of three notes.

clue.text: Soldiers not necessarily Brazilian

blocks.note: surface reading: troops that may or may not come from Brazil
setter's reading: Pará is a Brazilian state, so soldiers whose name begins with it sound Brazilian though they need not be

explanation.walkthrough: Pará is a state in northern Brazil, so the parachute soldiers read as troops from Pará.
explanation.definitionFit: Paratroops are soldiers trained to drop into action by parachute.

clue.text: Magistrate gets some leisure eventually?

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A busy judge will get some time off in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official or chief magistrate of a town or district in Anglo-Saxon and medieval England.

clue.text: Philosopher returns the Spanish babies to Republicans

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the whole string of pieces is read from the end

blocks.note: el is the Spanish word for the
tots are small children
the Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: A thinker sends Spanish infants back to the republican side.
explanation.walkthrough: IRA is the Irish Republican Army, so 'Republicans' gives three letters rather than R.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek thinker, pupil of Plato, so he is a philosopher.

clue.text: But not where barristers used to enjoy refreshers

definitions.text: But not where barristers used to enjoy refreshers

blocks.clueFragment: But not where barristers used to enjoy refreshers
blocks.note: surface reading: a pub where lawyers went for drinks

blocks.clueFragment: But not where barristers used to enjoy refreshers
blocks.note: setter's reading: a London landmark beside the Inns of Court whose name contains bar, though it was never a drinking bar

explanation.walkthrough: A refresher is an extra fee paid to a barrister; the Temple is home to two Inns of Court, and Temple Bar was the gateway into the City of London there.
explanation.definitionFit: Temple Bar was the ceremonial gateway on Fleet Street beside the Temple, the London legal quarter.

clue.text: Spirit heater, a pound

blocks.note: the heating element of a kettle or fire
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A spirit stove that costs one pound.
explanation.definitionFit: An elemental is a nature spirit, one of the beings once believed to inhabit earth, air, fire or water.

clue.text: Irish poet wandering in Meath with aunt

indicators.note: wandering means roaming about, so the letters stray from their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet from Ireland roams County Meath accompanied by his aunt.
explanation.walkthrough: Meath is an Irish county, which makes the surface scene apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum Tate was a Dublin-born writer who became English Poet Laureate in 1692.

clue.text: A success with a bird - egghead Uriah

blocks.note: a hit is a success
a tit is a small songbird
read as egg-head, the head or first letter of egg

explanation.surface: A clever brainy man called Uriah has a hit with a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah the Hittite is the soldier in the Bible whose wife Bathsheba David took; 'egghead' splits into egg and head.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament Uriah is identified by his people, the ancient Anatolian nation of the Hittites.

clue.text: Episcopal joint?

blocks.note: surface reading: a joint of meat or a place belonging to a bishop
setter's reading: the word for a bishop's tall hat is also a corner joint in carpentry

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: the same word names a bishop's headdress and a woodworking joint cut at 45 degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop wears this tall pointed hat, and carpenters use the same word for an angled corner join.

clue.text: One lot gets upset about rent in the Lebanon

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, which in a down clue turns the letters upside down
about means surrounding, so the overturned letters go round the next word

blocks.note: the Roman numeral one
taken as written
a rip is a tear or rent

explanation.surface: A single group is disturbed over the rent in Lebanon.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a place: there is a Tripoli in Lebanon as well as the Libyan capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is a major port city in northern Lebanon, distinct from the Libyan capital of the same name.

clue.text: Tom has a point - bloody class!

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
east, a point of the compass
gory means bloody

explanation.surface: Tom makes a fair point about a wretched school class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' reads as the British mild swearword, but it is used literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A category and a class are both groups of things sharing a characteristic, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: The carving's arrived, love

blocks.note: came means arrived
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: The sculpture has arrived, darling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a small relief carving on a gem or shell, usually a profile head.

clue.text: Author goes wrong without direction

indicators.note: wrong means awry, so the letters are not in their right order
without in its old sense means outside, so the letters go round the direction

blocks.note: taken as written
south, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A writer loses his way because he has no sense of direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but here it means outside, wrapping round the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Gosse was an English critic and author, best known for the memoir Father and Son.

clue.text: Fish in locality of the sound

indicators.note: of the sound tells the solver to go by how a word is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: a locality is a place

explanation.surface: A fish found in some local stretch of water, a sound being an inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' also suggests a sea channel, a natural home for a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a European flatfish with orange spots, widely eaten in Britain.

clue.text: Ray's a member in the house

blocks.note: first meaning: a shaft of light
second meaning: a structural timber supporting a building

explanation.surface: Ray sits in Parliament as a Member of the House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member in the house' suggests an MP, but it is a structural member, a supporting piece of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam is a shaft of light, and also a long horizontal timber or girder holding up a building.

clue.text: Servant changed notes in county town

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters are put into another order

blocks.note: a maid is a female servant
taken as written

explanation.surface: A servant swapped some banknotes while in a provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: A county town is the administrative centre of an English county; MAIDSTONE is Kent's.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidstone is the administrative capital of Kent, which makes it that county's county town.

clue.text: Execrate a good man for showing push?

blocks.note: to boo is to jeer at or denounce
a saint is a good man, abbreviated St

explanation.surface: Cursing a decent man for being pushy.
explanation.walkthrough: ST for a saint, the 'good man', is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A boost is a push or lift that helps something upward or forward, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Overtaking beginners?

blocks.note: surface reading: drivers passing learners on the road
setter's reading: in cricket the first batsmen face the first overs, so they are beginners taking overs

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls; the pair who start an innings take the first of them, which is 'over-taking' at the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: The batsmen who start an innings in cricket face the first overs bowled, so they begin the play.

clue.text: Warlike old poet

blocks.note: first meaning: of or suited to war
second meaning: the Roman epigrammatist of the first century AD

explanation.surface: An aggressive bard from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes military or combative things, and the Latin epigram writer Marcus Valerius bore the same name.
